Get the blended respondents

Source: R/coverage.R
blend_data.Rd

blend_data() draws the synthetic respondents behind the best blend of an synthetic_coverage() or blend_llms() result: For each attempt, it takes from each model a share of its respondents that matches the blend weights and stacks them into one data frame. The model column names the model each respondent came from. Save the result with write_synthetic(), or benchmark it like any other synthetic data with as_synthetic_list(blended, model = "blend").

Usage

blend_data(x, n = NULL, attempts = NULL, seed = 1, synthetic = NULL)

Arguments

x

an sc_coverage object with a blend, from synthetic_coverage() or blend_llms().

n

respondents per attempt. NULL (the default) takes the smallest attempt among the models, as the blend's Structure does.

attempts

the attempts to draw from. NULL takes all of them.

seed

random seed for the draw.

synthetic

optional: The full synthetic data, as a named list in the form synthetic_coverage() takes, to draw the rows from, for example when the coverage was run on the item columns only and you want the persona columns too. It needs the same models, and each attempt the same number of rows in the same order. NULL uses the data stored in x.

Value

A tibble with one row per blended respondent: blend (the recipe, the same in every row), model (the source model), attempt, and the columns of the synthetic data. The weights are in the "weights" attribute.

Details

The draw is random, so seed makes it repeatable. Each model's respondents are drawn without replacement unless n asks for more than a model has.

See also

blend_llms(), synthetic_coverage(), write_synthetic()

Examples

set.seed(1)
a <- matrix(rlnorm(8, 0.2, 0.3)); d <- matrix(rnorm(8))
real <- as.data.frame(mirt::simdata(a, d, 600, itemtype = "dich"))
llm <- function(mu, s) lapply(1:4, function(i) as.data.frame(
  mirt::simdata(a, d, 150, itemtype = "dich", Theta = matrix(rnorm(150, mu, s)))))
cov <- synthetic_coverage(list(A = llm(0.8, 0.7), B = llm(-0.6, 0.9)), real)
blended <- blend_data(cov, seed = 2)
table(blended$model, blended$attempt)
#>    
#>      1  2  3  4
#>   A 75 75 75 75
#>   B 75 75 75 75
f <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv")
write_synthetic(blended, f)
